question: In the SpaceFibre lane initialisation state machine, what does a lane transmit while it is in the Connecting state, and what does it transmit in the Connected state?
claims: In the Connecting state the lane sends INIT2s.
In the Connected state the lane sends INIT3s.
reclassified_2026-08-18: Clause 5.5.2 states the state actions in normative prose ('When in the ... state the Lane Initialisation state machine shall initiate the following action: ... Send 32 LOST_SIGNAL control words'). Figure 5-29 illustrates; it does not carry the content. MY AUTHORING ERROR.

question: How long does a SpaceFibre lane remain in the ClearLine state before it moves on, and which state does it move to?
claims: The lane leaves ClearLine after 2 microseconds.
It moves from ClearLine to the Disabled state.
reclassified_2026-08-18: Same clause; 'ClearLine' and the 2 us timer both appear in the normative text of ECSS-E-ST-50-11. MY AUTHORING ERROR.

question: What does a SpaceFibre lane transmit in the LossOfSignal state, and what does it transmit in the PrepareStandby state?
claims: In the LossOfSignal state the lane sends 32 LOST_SIGNAL words.
In the PrepareStandby state the lane sends 32 STANDBY words.
reclassified_2026-08-18: Verified in clause 5.5.2 text verbatim. The pipeline answered it and cited 5.5.2. MY AUTHORING ERROR.

question: What condition takes a SpaceFibre lane from the Started state to the Connecting state?
claims: The lane moves from Started to Connecting on receiving 1023 words without error including at least one INIT1 or INIT2, or on FarEndActive.
reclassified_2026-08-18: '1023 words' appears in the normative text of ECSS-E-ST-50-11. MY AUTHORING ERROR.

question: Which signals does the Lane layer exchange with the Physical layer on a SpaceFibre multi-lane link?
claims: The Lane layer exchanges TX Symbols with the Physical layer.
The Lane layer exchanges 10-bit Parallel Data with the Physical layer.
The Lane layer drives Line Driver Enable and Line Receiver Enable.
The Lane layer drives CDR Enable.
The Physical layer reports Loss of Signal to the Lane layer.
reclassified_2026-08-18: Clause 5.5.1 and 6.4.2 name every Lane/Physical signal in text; the pipeline answered and cited them. MY AUTHORING ERROR.

question: When a spacecraft elapsed time (SCET) object is mapped into a CAN frame, which octets carry the Fine Time and which carry the Coarse Time?
claims: Fine Time occupies octets 1 to 3 of the SCET object.
Coarse Time occupies octets 4 to 7 of the SCET object.
why_figure_only: The struct in clause 7.1.2e declares Coarse Time first, so the text implies the opposite order. The wire layout exists only in Figure 7-1.

question: What are the sizes of the Coarse Time and Fine Time fields in the spacecraft elapsed time (SCET) compound data type?
claims: Coarse Time is an unsigned 32-bit field.
Fine Time is an unsigned 24-bit field.
why_figure_only: CONTROL - stated verbatim in the struct in clause 7.1.2e, in the same passage as F-CA-0006's figure.

question: What value does the RXERR word counter take on LaneReset in SpaceFibre, and what is it used for?
claims: On LaneReset the RXERR word counter shall be zero.
The RXERR word counter is used to check the bit error rate on the lane.
why_figure_only: CONTROL - clause 5.5.2.2a and b, on the same page as Figure 5-29.

question: Is slight discoloration of a marking sleeve caused by minor overheating a cause of rejection?
claims: Slight discoloration due to minor overheating shall not be a cause of rejection.
It is treated as a process indicator in accordance with IPC/WHMA-A-620.
why_figure_only: CONTROL - clause 6.12.6.2b states the rule in text; only the visual threshold is in Figures 6-2 and 6-3.

question: When a spacecraft UTC object is mapped into a CAN frame, which octets carry the Day, the ms of Day and the submilliseconds of ms?
claims: Submilliseconds of ms occupies octets 1 to 2 of the UTC object.
ms of Day occupies octets 3 to 6 of the UTC object.
Day occupies octets 7 to 8 of the UTC object.
why_figure_only: Clause 7.1.3e says the objects 'shall be mapped into the CAN frame according to Figure 7-2' - a DELEGATING reference. The struct declares Day first, so the text implies the opposite order. Figure read at page 50 before authoring.
